content:
The text discusses the concept of running time in the context of sorting elements. Key points include:

1. **Scalability**: Sorting a larger number of elements (e.g., six times ten to the ninth elements) will take significantly longer than sorting a smaller number (e.g., six elements).
2. **Parameterization**: To analyze and understand the behavior of sorting time, it is common to parameterize the input size and express time as a function of the size of the elements being sorted.
3. **Upper Bounds**: It is important to establish upper bounds on the running time to provide a guarantee to the user. Knowing the maximum time a program will take (e.g., no more than three seconds) is more useful than knowing the minimum time (e.g., at least three seconds), as it ensures the program's performance in practical scenarios, such as real-time settings.

In summary, the focus is on understanding and guaranteeing the maximum running time of sorting algorithms to ensure reliability and usability.
